texts: bad: the parse hands the whole inventory to every single ledger — it ends up saying that each ledger records all three near-miss winters, which turns a total across the ledgers into three per ledger. Mark the reading as joint so the count stays with the set as a whole: 'Together, the ledgers record three near-miss winters.'

mixed: the blanket denial over every wraith is right and the near-miss winters are carried, but the rule drops the past tense, so it denies wraiths emerging in general rather than denying that any emerged in those winters — a translator slip, not something your wording caused. One optional improvement while you are here: 'in the near-miss winters' has no standard slot and had to be improvised, whereas 'during' has one — 'No wraith emerged during the near-miss winters.'
good. the bare plural 'apprentices' becomes a habit each apprentice has, and 'the near-miss winters' correctly picks out the specific three rather than winters at large.
